content:
Alex Chen: Quick follow-up to the dashboard RFC — we saw a perf regression on the big billing dashboard when RBAC filters are applied at query-time (high-cardinality joins).
Samira Patel: saw that in prod traces too, P95 token time spiked ~2.4x after adding org_role filters.
Miguel Ortiz: rough cause: RBAC predicates force the planner to disable some index merges + causes large hash joins.
Alex Chen: two high-level options: 1) push RBAC into precomputed/materialized views (role-scoped pre-aggregations), or 2) keep RBAC at query layer but add smarter pruning / predicate pushdown + caching.
Priya Desai: option 1 sounds great for read-heavy dashboards, but precomputing per-role explodes storage. we have ~6 roles x 120 tenants with custom roles => scale problem.
Samira Patel: right — we can't precompute every custom role. but we could precompute tenant-level aggregates and apply lightweight role filtering on top.
Miguel Ortiz: SQL example that is problematic:
```sql
SELECT d.metric, sum(v)
FROM metrics m
JOIN datasets d ON m.ds = d.id
LEFT JOIN role_map r ON r.user = $USER
WHERE m.ts BETWEEN ... AND r.can_view = true
GROUP BY d.metric
```
The join to role_map with user-dependent rows prevents grouped index usage.
Casey Lee: what if we encode permissions in a bitmap per-dataset and store as smallint flag on dataset row, then mask using bitops at query time? avoids join.
Priya Desai: byte flag approach is promising but we'd need consistent encoding for custom roles. custom role -> bit position mapping could be heavy.
Samira Patel: alternative: materialize tenant-level aggregates + maintain a small per-user ACL cache in Redis; apply ACL filtering in app layer before submitting SQL (i.e., remove rows we know user can't see).
Alex Chen: tradeoffs: app-layer filtering reduces DB complexity but adds network round-trip and potential staleness if ACLs change. we need <1s invalidation for role edits.
Miguel Ortiz: we can invalidate Redis ACLs via event bus on role changes; propagation is <= 200ms in current infra.
Casey Lee: caching layer helps, but dashboards with ad-hoc filters still need DB sided filtering. Could combine: tenant-agg + redis ACL prune + fallback DB filter for edge cases.
Samira Patel: also memory pressure: tenant-agg size grows with time windows. may need TTL + downsampled retention.
Alex Chen: perf target: maintain P95 latency within 1.15x of baseline for top-10 dashboards. storage delta should be <20% of current usage.
Priya Desai: operational concerns: index churn for materialized view refreshes during writes — can't block ingestion. use incremental/async refresh.
Miguel Ortiz: suggest phased plan: (A) implement Redis ACL cache + app-layer pruning, measure improvement; (B) create tenant-level materialized aggregates for top-10 dashboards with async refresh; (C) explore bitmap permission encoding for a pilot tenant.
Casey Lee: + add a query-explain gated flag so we can collect CVs for slow plans and auto-alert when predicate pushdown fails.
Samira Patel: ok to run pilot in staging with synthetic tenant ~5M rows. I'll own test harness.
Alex Chen: owners and next steps: Samira -> perf tests and staging pilot, Miguel -> proof-of-concept async MV refresh, Priya -> cost estimate for storage + infra, Casey -> design bitmap schema. I'll coordinate rollout plan and docs.
Jordan (infra-bot): reminder: RBAC-change events will publish to `rbac-events` topic once Priya's KMS ACL PR merges.
Samira Patel: timeline? Can we get an initial staging result in 2 weeks?
Alex Chen: yes — aim for measurement + perf dashboard in 2 weeks. I'll add a short RFC update summarizing this thread.
Casey Lee: :thumbsup:
Priya Desai: noted.
Miguel Ortiz: thanks, all.
Alex Chen: ending thread — will post RFC update and link test run.
